video.title: 14 BORING Businesses That Run Without a Single Employee

summary: Faceless listicle combining two lists: seven 'booked hour' self-serve space rentals (karaoke booth, tanning booth, nap pod, infrared sauna pod, private dog field, day office, golf simulator bay) and seven certificate-gated recurring trades (pool cleaning, chimney sweep, pest control, energy audit, arborist, landscaping, commercial cleaning). A composite character 'Harry' illustrates each path. Key takeaways: for space rentals, an online calendar plus expiring door code replaces staff and placement in a host venue on revenue share is key; for trades, a cheap certificate plus recurring contracts is the moat. Numbers are aggregated ranges, not first-hand.

speakers.name: Narrator
speakers.description: Faceless channel narrator (Harry's Stealth Wealth); 'Harry' is a story character

ideas.name: Karaoke booth on revenue share in a host venue
ideas.one_liner: Put a private karaoke room inside a bar or bowling alley, sold by the hour via online booking and an expiring keypad code.
ideas.business_model: Hourly room rental; 20-30% revenue share paid to host venue instead of rent
ideas.customer: Groups of friends wanting private karaoke in the evening
ideas.problem: No private place to sing without an audience
ideas.offer: One private hour (later 30-minute base unit) in a soundproof booth, self check-in by code

pricing.notes: Weekday afternoons 10-20% below peak; repriced to a 30-minute base unit with hourly as a discount.

acquisition_channels.details: Host venue (bar, bowling alley, entertainment complex) funnels its regulars; revenue share 20-30%.

quote.text: You offer the host a share of the takings instead of rent, somewhere in the 20 to 30% range
quote.speaker: Narrator

acquisition_channels.details: Local search for 'karaoke room near me'.

ideas.delivery: Booth installed in host venue; online calendar generates a code per booking that expires at slot end; 15-minute buffers; no staff.
unit_economics_claims: With drinks/snacks operators report $1,100-4,000 per week

acquisition.how: Inbound local search plus host venue footfall; listings and ads automatable.

onboarding.how: Online booking calendar issues the slot and door code.

delivery.how: Booth runs itself; cleaning/reset between groups and host coordination are human.

support.how: FAQs and rebooking automated; damage/lockouts need a human or host venue.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in UK venues; UK needs music licensing (PPL PRS) for public karaoke, and host venue alcohol licence. Revenue share with pubs plausible.

risks: Utilisation risk; most walk-ups want 30-45 minutes

quotes.text: A room like that costs about 15 dollars an hour to run. It rents for 50 to 150. That gap is the whole business
quotes.speaker: Narrator

ideas.name: Self-serve tanning booth in a gym
ideas.one_liner: A sunless or UV tanning booth placed inside an existing gym, booked and paid per session.
ideas.customer: Gym members and locals wanting a tan before/after work
ideas.problem: Tanning salons are staffed and seasonal

acquisition_channels.details: Placed inside an existing gym; members are the footfall.

ideas.delivery: Booth with scheduling app; operator replaces lotion/bulbs.
unit_economics_claims: Big chains average ~$500,000/year per staffed location

acquisition.how: Host gym provides customers; online booking automatable.

onboarding.how: Online booking calendar issues the slot and door code.

delivery.how: Machine delivers; restocking and bulb maintenance are physical.

support.how: FAQs and rebooking automated; damage/lockouts need a human or host venue.

uk_applicability.notes: UK: Sunbeds (Regulation) Act 2010 bans under-18s and unsupervised sunbeds in England and Wales, so unmanned UV sunbeds are effectively illegal; sunless spray booths are possible.

risks: UK law bans unsupervised sunbed use (Sunbeds Regulation Act 2010)
Health rules on bulbs, signage, minimum ages

quotes.text: Health rules on bulb replacement, signage, and minimum ages mean a casual operator cannot just drop a bed into a spare room
quotes.speaker: Narrator

acquisition.how: Footfall comes from host building; host deal is human.

onboarding.how: Online booking calendar issues the slot and door code.

support.how: FAQs and rebooking automated; damage/lockouts need a human or host venue.

ideas.name: Private dog field rental (pay-to-play dog park)

tactics.name: Host-venue revenue share instead of rent
steps: Place the unit (booth, pod, bay) inside a venue with existing footfall
Pay the host 20-30% of takings instead of fixed rent
Online booking calendar generates an expiring door code per booking

quote.text: Put 15 minutes of buffer between every booking from day one
quote.speaker: Narrator

tactics.name: Price the unit customers want
steps: Check real utilisation vs booked hours
Make the hourly rate the discount for staying longer

quote.text: Price the unit the customer actually wants to buy, not the unit that is easiest to bill
quote.speaker: Narrator

tactics.name: Three filters before buying a unit
steps: Does the crowd already walk past the door?
Can the space be reset without you?
Which hours does it fill; stack units whose peak hours differ

quote.text: Does the crowd already walk past the door? If the answer is no, that is a marketing problem being bought
quote.speaker: Narrator

tactics.name: 10-minute demand check on maps
steps: Search maps for nearest karaoke room, golf bay and private dog field
Check distance and whether their calendars have free evening slots this week

tactics.name: Certificate moat plus recurring contract
steps: Pick a trade with a cheap fast certificate
Sell a recurring contract (weekly/quarterly/nightly) not one-off jobs
Use a one-page scope and term contract for every account

quote.text: He wrote a simple scope and term contract for every account after that
quote.speaker: Narrator

warnings.warning: Chasing one-off jobs instead of recurring contracts.

UK: unsupervised UV sunbeds are banned; door-to-door and cold calling to homes need TPS checks under PECR; cold SMS to homeowners is illegal without consent.

lessons.lesson: The calendar and the expiring lock replace the employee for space-rental businesses.

quote.text: The calendar is the business. And the lock is the employee
quote.speaker: Narrator

lessons.lesson: Utilisation, not sticker price, decides unit economics.

quote.text: Utilization, not the sticker price, is what decides this
quote.speaker: Narrator

lessons.lesson: Stack units whose demand peaks at different hours in one footprint.
Revenue share with a host turns fixed rent into a variable cost.
A cheap certificate most competitors skip can be the moat.

quote.text: The trade is not the moat. The certificate is
quote.speaker: Narrator

lessons.lesson: Never sign a recurring contract at a price you cannot service twice.

quote.text: Never sign a recurring contract at a price you cannot service twice
quote.speaker: Narrator

lessons.lesson: A business is worth more the less the owner is required (Built to Sell).
Route density drives profit in service routes.

evidence_quality.rationale: Second-hand aggregated ranges and a composite fictional character; some named operators but no first-hand interviews.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Mentions books (Built to Sell, So Good They Can't Ignore You); no product sold.
